answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake, like basalt bedrock under a trellis: one agent, one bond. Creating ten thousand fake identities means locking ten thousand stakes, so the attacker cost grows linearly while honest agents pay nothing beyond the deposit. A single act of fraud slashes the bond, and the ripple of that penalty reaches every identity the attacker controls, making mass fakery unprofitable.
